solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Dairy product delivered by Dutch airline travelling west across India

indicators.note: across reads left to right, so heading west means running right to left, backwards
lying across something means straddling it, so one piece spans another

blocks.note: KLM is the Dutch national airline
India is I in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: A milk delivery arrives on a KLM flight heading west over India.
explanation.walkthrough: The airline's initials turn round to MLK, then straddle I for India to give M-I-LK.
explanation.definitionFit: Milk is the basic dairy item from which cheese, butter and cream are all made.

clue.text: Force male boat crew to jettison leader

indicators.note: jettisoning the leader means throwing off whatever stands at the front

blocks.note: M is the standard abbreviation for male
a rowing eight is a crew of eight oarsmen

explanation.surface: A coach forces the men's rowing crew to throw their captain overboard.
explanation.walkthrough: An eight in rowing is both the boat and its crew; dropping its first letter leaves IGHT after M.
explanation.definitionFit: Might is power or strength, as in the saying that might makes right, so it matches force.

clue.text: Following regular rejections, client with cute bum leaves

indicators.note: rejecting at regular intervals throws out every other letter, keeping the rest
as an adjective bum means faulty or worthless, so the letters are in poor order
with means alongside, so one piece is simply set next to another

blocks.note: the second, fourth and sixth letters of client
taken as written, then rearranged

explanation.surface: After several knock-backs, a customer with a pretty bottom walks out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Leaves' reads as a verb, someone departing, but it is a noun: the leaves of a salad plant. 'Bum' is American slang for faulty, which signals the shuffle.
explanation.definitionFit: Lettuce is a salad vegetable eaten as its green leaves, so leaves is a loose description of it.

clue.text: Victorian playwright’s massive carriage reportedly out of control

indicators.note: reportedly means as people say it, so the word is given by its sound

blocks.note: OS stands for outsize, a clothing size
a railway car is a carriage
something wild is out of control; the surname is said the same way

explanation.surface: A nineteenth-century dramatist's enormous coach is said to have run away with him.
explanation.walkthrough: OS (outsize) and CAR are spelt as given; only the last part changes spelling, WILD becoming the playwright's surname WILDE.
explanation.definitionFit: Oscar Wilde wrote The Importance of Being Earnest and other comedies staged in the 1890s, during Queen Victoria's reign.

clue.text: Heads of security hurry towards the back passage

indicators.note: the heads of words are their first letters, so only those are kept

blocks.note: the opening letters of the two words
aft means towards the stern, the back of a ship

explanation.surface: Security chiefs rush to the rear corridor.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Heads of security' sounds like senior guards, but it takes the first letters of two words; AFT is the nautical word for the rear.
explanation.definitionFit: A shaft is a narrow vertical passage, such as a mine shaft or a lift shaft.

clue.text: Abruptly, Ian Thorpe swims around Dutch Olympian

indicators.note: stopping abruptly means being cut off short, so the end is lost
when your head swims everything moves about, so the letters are mixed
going around something means enclosing it on both sides

blocks.note: taken as written, then cut short
taken as written
D is the abbreviation for Dutch

explanation.surface: Australian champion swimmer Ian Thorpe suddenly laps a Dutch Olympic athlete.
explanation.walkthrough: Ian Thorpe really was an Olympic swimmer, so 'Olympian' looks like an athlete; here it means one of the gods of Mount Olympus.
explanation.definitionFit: Aphrodite, Greek goddess of love, was one of the twelve gods who lived on Mount Olympus.

clue.text: Lead character in Rainbow wearing tight gown that’s inappropriate

indicators.note: the leading character of a word is its first letter
tight is slang for drunk, and drunken letters stagger out of order
whoever wears clothes is inside them, so one piece goes within the other

blocks.note: the first letter of Rainbow
taken as written, then rearranged

explanation.surface: The star of a children's show called Rainbow wears a figure-hugging dress that is unsuitable.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tight gown' reads as a close-fitting dress, but tight means drunk and scrambles the gown's letters around R.
explanation.definitionFit: Wrong can mean unsuitable or improper for the occasion, the same sense as inappropriate.

clue.text: Freckles of setter disappear after 40 days of fasting

indicators.note: coming after something means being placed behind it in the line

blocks.note: Lent is the forty-day Christian fast before Easter
the setter refers to themself as I
to go is to vanish or leave

explanation.surface: The setter hopes their freckles will fade after Lent.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'of' after Freckles is only a link; the setter-as-I convention supplies the middle. The answer is a medical term most solvers will reach only through the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: Lentigo is the medical term for small flat brown skin spots, including freckles, so it can stand for them collectively.

clue.text: Naked men run into New York, getting caught, resulting in disaster

indicators.note: naked means stripped of its outer covering, so only the inside is kept
getting something means taking it in, so one piece receives another

blocks.note: the middle letter once the outside letters are stripped
to run into one another is to merge
NY is the abbreviation for New York
C is the cricket scorecard abbreviation for caught

explanation.surface: Streakers dash into New York, are arrested, and chaos follows.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Naked men' is the picture of streakers, but it strips MEN down to E; 'run into' is one unit meaning MERGE.
explanation.definitionFit: An emergency is a sudden crisis demanding urgent action, close in sense to a calamity or disaster.

clue.text: A top company detains extremists in uncivil Mexican city

indicators.note: to detain someone is to hold them inside, so one piece is held within another
the extremes of a word are its two outermost letters

blocks.note: taken as written
a cap is a top or lid
CO is the abbreviation for company
the first and last letters of uncivil

explanation.surface: A leading firm holds militants in a lawless Mexican town.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Extremists' sounds like militants, but it means the end letters of the next word; CO then holds those two letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Acapulco is a resort port on Mexico's Pacific coast, famous for its cliff divers.

clue.text: Barge into audience by accident

blocks.note: the gate is the number of spectators at a sports match
a crash is a collision or accident

explanation.surface: Accidentally pushing your way into a crowd of spectators.
explanation.walkthrough: 'By accident' looks like a phrase meaning unintentionally, but 'by' only joins, and accident gives the second word. GATE is British sporting usage for a crowd.
explanation.definitionFit: To gatecrash is to enter a party or event uninvited, pushing in where you are not welcome.

clue.text: Small piece of skinned cod Mum’s brother left unused

indicators.note: skinning removes the outer layer, so only the middle survives
what is unused plays no part, so it is dropped from the result

blocks.note: the middle letter once the outer letters go
your mother's brother is your uncle
L is the abbreviation for left; it is the letter taken out

explanation.surface: A small bit of filleted cod was left uneaten by Mum's brother.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Left unused' reads as leftovers, but 'left' is L, which drops out of UNCLE.
explanation.definitionFit: An ounce is a tiny amount, as in 'not an ounce of sense', besides being a small unit of weight.

clue.text: Proclaim the President in America and in France

indicators.note: and simply adds one thing to the next in a line

blocks.note: Donald Trump is the American President
et is French for and

explanation.surface: An announcement of the President, in the USA and in France.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'and' does double duty: it joins the two parts and is also the word translated as ET by 'in France'.
explanation.definitionFit: To trumpet something is to announce it loudly and publicly, as if blowing a fanfare.

clue.text: One cuts, with seconds to go, two songs in progress

indicators.note: things that are to go are being removed, so they are taken out
something that cuts into another splits it and sits in the gap

blocks.note: song twice over
s is short for second, and both of them are removed
the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A DJ trims the setlist with seconds remaining, two songs still playing.
explanation.walkthrough: Remove both S's from SONG SONG to leave ONGONG; then I splits it after the fourth letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Ongoing describes something still continuing and not yet finished, the same idea as in progress.

clue.text: Oil company beginning to search somewhere underground?

indicators.note: the beginning of a word is its first letter

blocks.note: the first letter of search
hell is traditionally imagined beneath the earth

explanation.surface: A petroleum firm starts exploring for deposits below ground.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags that 'somewhere underground' is a playful description of the underworld, not a real oilfield.
explanation.definitionFit: Shell is one of the world's largest petroleum businesses, an Anglo-Dutch multinational.

clue.text: Large reptile turns over egg and starts to search around under rocks

indicators.note: turning over flips a thing end to end
and adds one thing to the next in a row
the start of each word is its first letter

blocks.note: to turn nasty is to get nasty, so turns can mean becomes, or gets
an egg is shaped like the letter O
the first letters of these four words

explanation.surface: A huge lizard flips its egg and goes hunting under some stones.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Turns over' looks like one phrase about flipping the egg, but 'turns' gives GETS and 'over' reverses it.
explanation.definitionFit: A stegosaur is a dinosaur with bony back plates; dinosaurs were huge prehistoric reptiles.

clue.text: Friend at the west end of Northampton, perhaps for a movie

indicators.note: the west end is the left side, so this goes first in the line

blocks.note: Cockney rhyming slang: china plate means mate, a friend
Northampton is an English town; 'perhaps' marks it as one example

explanation.surface: A friend is in the west of Northampton, maybe to see a film.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The west end' suggests a district of the town, but it only places the friend to the left of TOWN.
explanation.definitionFit: Chinatown is the 1974 Roman Polanski film noir starring Jack Nicholson.

clue.text: Dave’s partner is caught by Edward and punished

indicators.note: something caught is held inside its captor

blocks.note: Chas and Dave were a British cockney pub-rock duo
taken as written
Ted is a short form of Edward

explanation.surface: Dave's companion is arrested by Edward and disciplined.
explanation.walkthrough: The little word 'is' does double duty as letters and as part of the containment phrase. Chas and Dave were a London singing double act known for cockney pub songs.
explanation.definitionFit: To chastise is to scold or discipline severely, so chastised and punished are synonyms.

clue.text: Hands and feet of each character (except John) close to Jesus

indicators.note: the close of a word is its end, so only its final letter is kept

blocks.note: every character of a four-letter name is all four of them; the bracket is the setter's teasing aside
the last letter of Jesus

explanation.surface: A religious image of every figure except John at Jesus's side, hands and feet shown.
explanation.walkthrough: The wordplay is loose: 'each character' is read as ALL FOUR, then S from the end of Jesus.
explanation.definitionFit: Being on all fours means resting on both hands and both feet or knees, like a crawling child.

clue.text: Ornate pants tear after old boy with beer does a back flip

indicators.note: a back flip turns things backwards, end over end
pants is British slang for rubbish, so the letters are a mess
placed after means coming behind in the line

blocks.note: OB is the abbreviation for old boy, a former pupil
ale is a type of beer
taken as written, then rearranged

explanation.surface: A fancy pair of trousers rips when an old schoolboy, drink in hand, does a backflip.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pants' looks like trousers, but it is British slang for rubbish and shuffles TEAR. OB plus ALE runs backwards as ELABO.
explanation.definitionFit: Elaborate means intricately detailed and richly decorated, which is what ornate describes.

clue.text: In the morning I see bats are gathered across the pond

indicators.note: bats means crazy, so the letters go wild and rearrange

blocks.note: am stands for ante meridiem, before noon
I see said as letters, I and C
taken as written

explanation.surface: In the morning I see bats roosting together on the far side of the lake.
explanation.walkthrough: The bats look like animals, but bats means mad and scrambles IC plus ARE. 'I see' becomes IC by the sound of the two letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Across the pond is a British idiom for the United States, the pond being the Atlantic Ocean.

clue.text: Cuckoo to fly high

indicators.note: cuckoo means crazy, and crazy letters fall out of order

blocks.note: taken as written, then rearranged

explanation.surface: A cuckoo taking off to soar up into the sky.
explanation.walkthrough: Cuckoo looks like the bird about to fly, but it means mad.
explanation.definitionFit: Lofty means of great height or towering, so it is a synonym for tall or elevated.

clue.text: Act with the woman getting a part in The Seagull?

blocks.note: a feat is a deed or act
her refers to a woman

explanation.surface: An actress lands a role in Chekhov's play The Seagull.
explanation.walkthrough: The Seagull is Chekhov's play, so 'a part' reads as a role; the question mark lets it mean a literal part of a gull.
explanation.definitionFit: A feather is one of the many pieces making up a gull's plumage, so it is literally a part of the bird.

clue.text: Gorge on food served late in the day after cycling

indicators.note: coming after means being placed behind in the line
cycling sends letters round, the front one moving to the back

blocks.note: over can mean on top of, as on does

blocks.clueFragment: food served late in the day
blocks.note: tea is a light afternoon meal in Britain

explanation.surface: Stuffing yourself with an evening meal after a long bike ride.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Gorge on' wants to be the definition, but 'on' gives OVER; TEA, an afternoon or evening meal in Britain, has its T moved to the end.
explanation.definitionFit: To gorge is to stuff yourself greedily, which is to eat too much.

clue.text: Bushes forming boundaries, but not hard boundaries

indicators.note: but not means excluding, so something is removed

blocks.note: hedges are rows of bushes marking a boundary
H is the pencil abbreviation for hard

explanation.surface: Shrubs marking field borders, though not the solid ones like walls.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Boundaries' appears twice: the first is part of the hedge description, the second the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Edges are the outer limits or borders of something, so they are its boundaries.

clue.text: Desire of kinky masochist is suppressed

indicators.note: something suppressed is held down and kept out of sight
kinky means twisted, so the letters are bent into a new shape

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written; these letters are removed

explanation.surface: A deviant masochist's longing is kept hidden.
explanation.walkthrough: Remove I and S from masochist and twist the seven remaining letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Stomach as a noun means appetite or inclination, as in having no stomach for a fight.

clue.text: Bass part’s range

blocks.note: first meaning: one of the small plates on a fish such as a sea bass
second meaning: extent or spread

explanation.walkthrough: Bass suggests the low voice part in music, and range then sounds like vocal range; the bass is really a fish.
explanation.definitionFit: Fish skin is covered in protective plates, and the word also means the extent or spread of something.

clue.text: Sweetie (humbug?) quietly binned

indicators.note: something binned has been thrown away

blocks.note: humbug is fraud or nonsense, so a phoney thing
p is the musical mark piano, meaning quietly

explanation.surface: A sweet, perhaps a humbug, is quietly thrown away.
explanation.walkthrough: A humbug is also a British boiled mint sweet, which is why it sits beside 'Sweetie'; here it means fraud.
explanation.definitionFit: Honey is a term of endearment, used like sweetie or darling for someone loved.

clue.text: Getting old silver in the back of Jag

indicators.note: the back of a word is its last letter

blocks.note: Ag is the chemical symbol for silver
taken as written
the final letter of Jag

explanation.surface: Going grey, sitting in the back seat of a Jaguar.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Getting old silver' reads as tarnished metal, but the definition stops at 'old'. A Jag is a Jaguar car.
explanation.definitionFit: Aging, the American spelling of ageing, means growing older over time.

clue.text: Endlessly looking around you for spiny-skinned creature

indicators.note: without an end means the final letter is cut off
going around something encloses it

blocks.note: searching is looking for something
U is text-speak for you

explanation.surface: Forever hunting about for a prickly animal.
explanation.walkthrough: SEARCHIN, with its last letter gone, holds U after the third letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A sea urchin is a marine echinoderm covered in sharp spines; echinoderm literally means spiny skin.

clue.text: Harps broken by Solomon during lyrical works/pieces

indicators.note: something broken is in pieces and gets reassembled differently
by means beside, so one part stands next to another
during means within the span of, so one piece sits inside

blocks.note: taken as written, then rearranged
odes are lyric poems
Solomon is the setter, who calls themself I

explanation.surface: Harps were wrecked by King Solomon in the middle of singing psalms.
explanation.walkthrough: Solomon is this puzzle's setter, so he is I, placed inside ODES. The slash splits the wordplay from the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A rhapsody is a free-form musical composition, an emotional single-movement piece such as Liszt's Hungarian Rhapsodies.

clue.text: Soldiers hiding in farmyard

indicators.note: something hiding in a place is tucked inside it, so look within the letters

blocks.note: the second to fifth letters of farmyard

explanation.surface: Troops lying low in a farmyard.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer sits inside a single word, f-ARMY-ard.
explanation.definitionFit: An army is a large organised body of soldiers, so the word collects them as a group.
